Here, we need to substitute each vector into the given matrix differential equation and check if it results in a true statement.

For ${x}_{1}(t)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}({e}^{t})^{′} \\ ({e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for ${x}_{2}(t)$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}({e}^{t})^{′} \\ (0)^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for ${x}_{3}(t)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}(0)^{′} \\ ({e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{3}(t)$ only".
